newsitem.title: USA: Kmart posts best operating results in four years.
newsitem.headline: Kmart posts best operating results in four years.

text.p: Kmart Corp. said Wednesday that cost-cutting allowed it to slash its fourth-quarter net losses by 61 percent and post its best full-year profit from continuing operations in four years.

The fourth-quarter net loss, which included write-offs and losses from Kmart's discontinued Builders Square unit, came to $164 million, or 27 cents a share, compared with a year-earlier loss of $420 million, or 91 cents a share.
Revenues fell to $9.68 billion from $9.9 billion a year earlier.

Excluding the Builders Square losses, Kmart's core discount store operations earned a fourth-quarter profit of $235 million, compared with a year-ago loss of $118 million. For the full fiscal 1996 year ended Jan. 29, Kmart's continuing operations earned $231 million, compared with a fiscal 1995 loss of $431 million.
"One year ago we pledged a major financial and strategic restructuring of the company," Kmart Chairman Floyd Hall said in a statement.

"We indicated that the financial decline of Kmart had bottomed and that we would return the company to profitability in 1996. These results, which are Kmart's best earnings from continuing operations in the past four years, make good on that promise to our shareholders," he said.

Kmart's fiscal 1996 revenues dipped to $31.44 billion from $31.71 billion in fiscal 1995, putting Kmart in third place among the nation's top retailers, behind Wal-Mart Stores Inc. and Sears, Roebuck & Co.

Most of the retailer's improvement came from cost cuts. It reduced selling, general and administrative expenses in 1996 by $602 million from 1995 to a total of $6.27 billion, or about 19.9 percent of sales.
Kmart said such expenses for the full-year fell below 20 percent of sales for the first time in 25 years, and compared with 21.7 percent in 1995.
But Hall said he was disappointed with Kmart's slow improvements in same-store sales, or sales from stores open at least a year, and gross profit margins.

"The challenge for 1997 is clear," he said. "We must improve our marketing and operational initiatives to drive increased sales. In the coming year, Kmart will exert every effort to improve its assortments, store appearance and customer service."
Kmart's gross profit margin for the full year was 22.4 percent of sales vs. 22.2 percent in 1995. Gross margin for the fourth quarter was 21.6 percent of sales vs. 21.0 percent a year earlier.

Kmart's operating results exceeded analysts' consensus estimates, but a company spokesman cautioned that part of that difference was attributable to a lower-than-expected tax rate of about 20.5 percent due to foreign tax benefits.

In addition, the fourth-quarter results from continuing operations included a $108 million pre-tax gain on the sale of Kmart's stock in Rite Aid Corp., which was partially offset by a $98 million charge to write down the value of Kmart's international operations.
Continuing operations results in the fiscal 1995 fourth quarter included after-tax non-cash accounting charges of $150 million.
Kmart shares were up 25 cents at $13.125 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
